We have applied template 1914393 to target, got two fragments: product? Actually retrosynthesis: applying template yields precursors. The result tuple: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So first precursor is aromatic part with amide and triazine? Actually it's COc1... etc. Second is a heterocycle with F and CCl substituent.

Now apply template 1914394 to second precursor 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1' gave precursors: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So we get dichloromethane? Actually ClCCl is Cl-CH2-Cl? That's dichloromethane. And the other is same heterocycle but phenyl instead of chlorophenyl.

Now we need to apply template 1914395 to something. Likely to the first precursor? Let's see template 1914395 is a fluorination of a heterocycle? The retro template: O-[CH;D3;+0:1]1-[C:2]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-1>>[F;D1;H0:5]-[CH;D3;+0:1]1-[C:2]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-1. So it breaks a C-F bond to give an OH? Actually forward: O-CH... -> F-CH... So retro: from F-CH... to O-CH... So we need a precursor with F-CH... to get OH-CH... So maybe apply to the heterocycle with F? The second precursor after step2 is 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1' which has F attached to carbon of ring. Applying template 1914395 to that should give an alcohol precursor: O-CH... So let's apply.
